name: Token stream
description: Immediate token-like delivery for conversational responses. Partial words are allowed, as in real model streams.
sample:
A well-designed interface makes uncertainty easier to manage. When a system needs time to prepare an answer, a small and meaningful signal can reassure the reader that their request has been received. As the response begins to appear, the words that have already arrived should remain stable, allowing someone to read at their own pace without being distracted by unnecessary movement.

The goal is not to make the interface feel faster than it really is, but to make the waiting experience feel understandable and predictable.

The dashboard redesign has reached its first internal milestone. The core experience is in place, with navigation and account discovery identified as the remaining priorities.

Project update — November

[[We have completed a lot of work on the dashboard, and the team is happy with the direction. There are still a few problems with the navigation that we need to solve.

Next milestone: share the revised prototype with the wider team.

name: Section assembly
description: Deliver whole sections with headings and supporting prose as coherent blocks.
sample:
Overview
The dashboard should help customers understand their current financial commitments without navigating through multiple product screens.

Key findings
Customers frequently look for documents, repayment information, and payment actions. These tasks should remain visible and predictable.

Next steps
Prototype the updated hierarchy, test it with representative users, and measure task completion before finalizing the release.

name: Checklist assembly

[ ] Identify recurring navigation and account discovery problems.
[ ] Prototype a simpler repayment and document experience.
[ ] Validate the changes with representative customers.

name: Quoted passages
description: Reveal complete passages with temporary emphasis on the incoming excerpt.
sample:

name: Progressive explanation
description: Deliver complete explanatory sentences without distracting motion.
sample: The experience should begin with the information that matters most to the customer. Secondary actions can remain available without competing with the primary task. This hierarchy reduces unnecessary navigation and makes the interface easier to understand.

name: List token stream
description: A continuous list stream for short items; a caret marks the current insertion point.
sample:
Recommended next steps

1. Review the customer journey and identify the points where people are most likely to need assistance.
2. Prioritize the actions that resolve the most common issues without adding unnecessary navigation.
3. Test the revised interface with a small group of customers and record where they hesitate.
4. Refine the design based on observed behavior before expanding the release.
